categories.main_business_segments: Fuji Co., Ltd. operates primarily as a comprehensive retailer, with its main business being supermarkets under various brands (Fuji, MaxValu, MaruNaka, The Big, etc.) across western Japan. The group also includes related businesses such as food processing, logistics, real estate leasing, fitness clubs, restaurants, travel agencies, and financial services (electronic money and card services).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced retail management systems, supply chain integration, and digital transformation (DX) initiatives such as electronic shelf labels and self-checkout systems. Food processing and logistics are supported by centralized process centers for fresh and prepared foods, with a focus on HACCP-based food safety management. The company also emphasizes energy-efficient store operations and sustainability practices.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Fuji primarily serves general consumers in the regions where its stores operate, targeting households and individuals seeking daily necessities, groceries, and lifestyle products. Its customer base is broad, encompassing all age groups, with a particular focus on local communities in western Japan. The company also provides services to tenants (real estate leasing) and business partners through its B2B operations.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s core operations are concentrated in the Chugoku, Shikoku, and western Hyogo regions of Japan, with a network of over 400 stores spanning prefectures such as Ehime, Hiroshima, Okayama, Yamaguchi, Kagawa, Tokushima, Kochi, and Hyogo. The group has no significant overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Fuji operates primarily at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer, directly serving end consumers. It also has midstream functions through its food processing subsidiaries and logistics centers, and upstream activities via agricultural subsidiaries and procurement integration with Aeon Group.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include establishing a unified corporate culture, reforming existing businesses, integrating and optimizing business infrastructure, and advancing ESG management. Key initiatives involve digital transformation for operational efficiency, expanding private brand and original product development, supply chain integration, and sustainability efforts such as carbon reduction and resource recycling. There is no significant in-house R&D; innovation is focused on business process improvement and product development.
categories.revenue_model: Fuji generates revenue primarily through the sale of goods at its retail stores (supermarkets, discount stores, specialty stores), as well as through real estate leasing, food processing, and ancillary services such as fitness clubs and travel agencies. Additional income streams include electronic money and card services, and tenant leasing fees.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Fuji is positioned as the leading super-regional retailer in the Chugoku and Shikoku regions, competing with other major Japanese supermarket chains such as Seven & i Holdings, Ito-Yokado, and regional players. As a consolidated subsidiary of Aeon, it benefits from group synergies but faces intense competition from both national chains and local supermarkets, as well as from discount and specialty retailers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending February 2025, Fuji reported consolidated sales of 778.2 billion yen, with operating profit of 12.95 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 3.82 billion yen. The company employs over 8,000 people (over 25,000 including part-time staff). Growth is stable but modest, with recent increases driven by mergers and store network expansion; however, profit margins have been pressured by rising costs and integration expenses.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Fuji emphasizes 'overwhelming safety and excitement' for customers and employees, focusing on community-based retailing, everyday low prices (EDLP), and a wide assortment of both national and private brand products. The company differentiates itself through local product offerings, original product development, and a strong commitment to ESG and sustainability, aiming to be the most community-contributing retailer in its regions.
